     1	# Task: GearVault — a multi-location equipment rental counter
     2	
     3	Build a small full-stack web app called **GearVault**. Three shop
     4	locations — Riverside, Downtown, and Harbour Pier — share one catalog of
     5	eighteen serialized units. Customers reserve cameras, lenses, drones,
     6	outdoor canvas, and event kit through Stripe Checkout; the shop checks
     7	the gear out and back in, and writes up damage against the deposit when
     8	something comes home wrong. After pay the till posts matching copies to
     9	the notice desk, the SMS desk, and the email desk; the fleet serial desk
    10	confirms bay codes before serial scans; and only members receive loyalty
    11	punches.
    12	
    13	What a booking costs is not simply the wall card times the days. The
    14	shop has its own week rate, the weekend desk and the county tax office
    15	disagree about what counts as part of a hire, and the insurance bureau
    16	bills by the day. This file is the whole brief. It is the shop talking,
    17	not a specification and not a checklist.
    18	
    19	`/assets/CREDENTIALS.md` covers Stripe, the shop Postgres, and the
    20	shop-network vendor desks. `/assets/artifacts/` holds the seed JSON, the
    21	riverside river mark, and the hire waiver PDF. Artifact money is whole
    22	dollars; the desks and the ledger work in pennies.
    23	
    24	Nothing in the product should need a route or an element id explained
    25	before it can be used.
    26	
    27	# GearVault — overview
    28	
    29	Build a small full-stack equipment rental counter. Customers find a
    30	serialized unit, pay the rental and deposit through Stripe's hosted
    31	Checkout, and can look back over their own bookings and certifications.
    32	Associates work the counter — kits go out and come back. Assessors write
    33	up what came home damaged. A shop manager decides what of the deposit
    34	that actually costs. A transfer clerk moves kits between the three shops
    35	when the transfer bureau will stamp the van. A bay technician issues
    36	serial scans. A night auditor reads the books without touching them.
    37	An insurance liaison reads hull binds. A lot runner fetches gear but does
    38	not drive the van.
    39	
    40	## Shape of the app
    41	
    42	It opens already signed in as the seeded customer **Maya Chen** — there is
    43	no registration, login, or password anywhere in the product — and a
    44	visible switcher moves between the seeded customers and staff. Customers
    45	reach a unit through a catalog and a profile, pay through Stripe's hosted
    46	Checkout, and have somewhere to find their own reservations, cards on
    47	file, paper receipts, texts, email copies, diary holds, and the punches
    48	on Maya's member card. Associates have somewhere to send a paid booking
    49	out the door and take it back — the door wants a live serial scan first,
    50	and the fleet serial desk must confirm the bay code before that scan
    51	ticket exists. Assessors have the return in front of them. The manager
    52	has the damage decision and the repair bay. The transfer clerk has the
    53	move between shops, and nothing else.
    54	
    55	## Seed accounts (first boot)
    56	
    57	Customers:
    58	
    59	| Name | Account | Notes |
    60	| --- | --- | --- |
    61	| Maya Chen | Active | Default. Current Drone Operator card through 2031-12-31. Member — the loyalty desk punches her card when a payment clears. |
    62	| Jordan Hale | Active | Drone Operator card expired 2024-03-01. Walk-in, not a member. |
    63	| Priya Nair | On hold | Unresolved damage balance. No drone card. |
    64	| Chris Nguyen | Active | No cards, no rental history, no texts, no email copies, no punches. |
    65	| Tess Okada | Active | Walk-in, not a member. No drone card. |
    66	| Luis Ferreira | Active | Walk-in, not a member. No drone card. |
    67	
    68	Staff:
    69	
    70	| Name | Role |
    71	| --- | --- |
    72	| Sam Ortiz | Rental Associate |
    73	| Dana Ruiz | Rental Associate |
    74	| Riley Okonkwo | Damage Assessor |

    81	| Casey Bloom | Lot Runner |
    82	
    83	Locations:
    84	
    85	| Shop | Notes |
    86	| --- | --- |
    87	| Riverside Rental Center | Riverside tax window (not the same as Downtown or Pier). |
    88	| Downtown Studio Annex | Downtown tax window. Cinema drones carry a bureau hull rider. |
    89	| Harbour Pier Desk | Pier tax window — lower rate than the other two shops. |
    90	
    91	Units (prefer the JSON under `/assets/artifacts/` when present — it carries
    92	stable ids). Money fields there are whole US dollars, so `400` means
    93	$400.00. All eighteen tags:
    94	
    95	| Tag | Category | Shop | Rate / day | Deposit | Replacement | Works | Status |
    96	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

   100	| B-216 | Boom Pole | Riverside | $18 | $40 | $220 | — | Available |
   101	| T-012 | Tent | Riverside | $25 | $80 | $220 | — | Available |
   102	| D-004 | Drone | Downtown | $120 | $500 | $2500 | Drone Operator | Available |
   103	| S-301 | PA Speaker | Downtown | $60 | $150 | $900 | — | In repair |
   104	| X-410 | Lighting Rig | Downtown | $90 | $300 | $2200 | — | Retired |
   105	| M-088 | Microphone | Downtown | $35 | $90 | $450 | — | Available |
   106	| Y-300 | Lighting Rig | Downtown | $55 | $120 | $700 | — | Available |
   107	| F-612 | Fog Machine | Downtown | $22 | $50 | $180 | — | Retired |
   108	| G-220 | Generator | Pier | $40 | $120 | $800 | — | Available |
   109	| R-090 | Rain Fly | Pier | $12 | $30 | $90 | — | Available |
   110	| P-330 | Projector | Pier | $70 | $200 | $1100 | — | Available |
   111	| C-077 | Camera Body | Pier | $50 | $150 | $900 | — | Available |
   112	| E-015 | PA Speaker | Pier | $48 | $110 | $640 | — | Available |
   113	| N-201 | Drone | Pier | $95 | $400 | $1800 | Drone Operator | Available |
   114	| H-019 | Hydrophone | Pier | $28 | $70 | $320 | — | Available |
   115	
   116	The shops do not invent tax, hull cover, weekend surcharges, weather
   117	holds, holiday closures, paid-ticket copies, texts, email copies, diary
   118	holds, serial scans, loyalty punches, fleet bay codes, or van moves
   119	themselves. Those live on vendor desks on the shop network (see `/assets/CREDENTIALS.md`). Riverside, Downtown, and Pier are not the same tax office, and
   120	that office knows the shops by the short names on the network, not the
   121	painted signs. The Pier window charges a lower percentage than Riverside
   122	or Downtown — a camera body quoted at the Pier with Downtown tax on the
   123	invoice was one of the fights last fall.
   124	
   125	What the county actually taxes is the kit line as the customer is
   126	invoiced for it — after the week rate, with the weekend line added in —
   127	and never the deposit or the bureau's hull rider. The week rate itself is
   128	the shop's own: from the seventh day on one paper a tenth comes off the
   129	kit line, six days is still full price, and the tenth never touches a
   130	deposit or the cover. Nothing goes on one paper for more than a
   131	fortnight. The Downtown drone carries a bureau hull rider and the Pier
   132	one does too; a tent does not — and the bureau bills that rider by the
   133	day, so it needs to be told how many days are on the paper. A Saturday or
   134	a Sunday on the paper picks up the weekend desk's line, once for each
   135	weekend day on it, so a Saturday-Sunday pair is twice a lone Saturday; a
   136	midweek span picks up nothing.
   137	
   138	Outdoor canvas — tent, generator, rain fly — stays in when the weather
   139	desk already called those days unsafe; the till has to listen to that
   140	call, not invent its own wording and send the kit anyway. The holiday
   141	desk already knows the week the shops go dark, and when the van is idle
   142	on those days the transfer bureau will not stamp a move; a quote that
   143	walked past that desk still printed a Checkout URL last Christmas. The
   144	weather desk looks at every day on the paper, not only the first. A kit
   145	out and back the same afternoon is still a day on the invoice. Booking
   146	dates are the calendar day on the paper, not a timestamp from whoever's
   147	laptop.
   148	
   149	After the card clears, the notice desk, the SMS desk, and the email desk
   150	are all supposed to hold the same ticket, the shop diary is supposed to
   151	show the hold, and Maya's member card is supposed to take a punch — a
   152	paper copy without the text, a text without the email, or an email
   153	without the punch is how last year's till got yelled at. Only members
   154	get loyalty punches; walk-ins do not, and Chris must not show punches
   155	when Maya paid. A Checkout nobody paid for leaves none of those behind.
   156	Nothing leaves the bay without a live serial scan, and the fleet serial
   157	desk must confirm the bay code before that scan ticket exists. A kit
   158	that has come home and not yet been inspected is not on the floor:
   159	nobody can book it and the van cannot take it. Noah is the only one the
   160	transfer bureau will talk to, and he only moves kit that is genuinely
   161	idle — not something already spoken for on a paid paper. Sam driving the
   162	van on a typed stamp is how a body ended up at the wrong shop. When
   163	Elena signs off a write-up Riley recorded as major, the kit goes to the
   164	repair bay rather than back onto the shelf. The books themselves live on
   165	the shop Postgres, not a local file, and they keep pennies even though
   166	the seed cards are whole dollars.
   167	
   168	If that directory is empty, keep the names, roles, tags, shops, rates,
   169	deposits, replacement values, certification flags, and statuses above, and
   170	invent stable ids.
   171	
   172	
   173	# How the shop works
   174	
   175	This is the shop talking about their business. It is not a specification and
   176	it does not describe an implementation. What the software has to guarantee is
   177	for you to work out.
   178	
   179	## Demo users
   180	
   181	- Seed the customers, staff, locations, units, and certifications from
   182	  `/assets/artifacts/`. Artifact money is given in whole dollars.
   183	- A fresh browser is already Maya Chen. A switcher changes who is using the
   184	  app. There are no passwords.
   185	- The switcher is there so the shop can demo the product to people.
   186	
   187	## Booking
   188	
   189	Customers book their own kits, in advance, and pay through Stripe before
   190	any date is actually held.
   191	
   192	## Notes from the shop manager
   193	
   194	We asked the shop manager what went wrong with the binder this replaces.
   195	She talked for the better part of an hour, poured more coffee, and this
   196	is roughly what she said. None of it was written down as a fault report,
   197	nobody ever established what was actually going on underneath, and in
   198	most cases the counter never worked out how to bring it about a second
   199	time. Take it as description rather than diagnosis. She jumped around.
   200	
   201	The calendar was the sore point. Two people showed up for the same 70-200
   202	on overlapping weekends — one had it through the 14th and the other was
   203	told they could have it from the 14th — and both pieces of paper were in
   204	the binder. Going the other way, a woman was refused a tent because she
   205	already had a camera body that same week, as if the tent and the body
   206	were the same physical thing, and another customer found that quoting a
   207	single weekend on the last lens appeared to swallow every other date on
   208	that lens; the shop manager was equally annoyed about both. Quotes also
   209	sat in the pile and blocked real walk-ins who were ready to pay, including
   210	at least one Checkout the customer opened and then abandoned on the train.
   211	Bookings went through for weekends that had already started — including at
   212	least one the system had apparently looked at and been perfectly happy
   213	with. A Friday-to-Sunday kit went on the invoice as two days, and the
   214	desk swears that camera is off the shelf all three.
   215	
   216	She is strict about how long one slip can run. Nothing goes out on a
   217	single paper for longer than a fortnight — fourteen days is the most the
   218	binder ever allowed and she wants that line held. The lens that sat in
   219	somebody's boot for six weeks started life as one open-ended slip that
   220	nobody had put an end to, and she is still angry about it. Fifteen days
   221	is not a booking; it is two bookings, and the customer can come back to
   222	the counter for the second one.
   223	
   224	Then she went off about Christmas. The shops were dark from the day
   225	before Christmas through Boxing Day, and again on New Year's Eve — the
   226	holiday desk on the shop network already had those days blocked, the
   227	same way the weather desk already knew about the November gales — and
   228	someone still printed a Checkout URL for a tent over Christmas week
   229	because the till never asked. A lens on those same dark days went out
   230	too. She said the holiday desk looks at every day on the paper, not
   231	only Christmas Day itself; a quote that started on a clear December
   232	afternoon and ran into the closed days was the one that made her
   233	shout. Midweek dates in September were fine. She did not write down
   234	the desk's address. She just kept saying "it already knew."
   235	
   236	## What the customer actually pays
   237	
   238	Finance stopped treating the wall-card sum as the whole Stripe total,
   239	and they do not treat a file on the tablet as the books — they read
   240	the shop Postgres IT already runs. The wall cards are still written in
   241	whole dollars; the books themselves keep the pennies, and more than one
   242	four-hundred-dollar lens deposit landed in the ledger as four dollars
   243	because someone copied the card number across as-is.
   244	
   245	The week rate is the part that took the longest to explain. A fortnight
   246	on the lens came out cheaper per day than the same lens for five days,
   247	and that is deliberate: the seventh day is where the week rate starts,
   248	and from there a tenth comes off the kit line. Six days is still every
   249	day at full price — she was very clear that the sixth day is not a
   250	week — and the seventh day takes the tenth off the whole slip, not
   251	just off the days past the sixth. The tenth comes off the kit line
   252	only. It has never come off a deposit, and the bureau does not discount
   253	cover because somebody hired for longer.
   254	
   255	That matters for the county, because the county taxes what the customer
   256	is actually being charged for the kit — the kit line the way it goes on
   257	the invoice, after the week rate has already come off it, with the
   258	weekend line added in, because as far as the county is concerned the
   259	weekend money is part of the hire. Finance had a long argument with
   260	them about that and lost. What the county does not touch is the
   261	deposit, which is the customer's own money coming back, and it does not
   262	touch the bureau's hull line either, which is insurance and taxed
   263	somewhere else entirely. A drone invoice that had been taxed on the
   264	whole bottom line, hull and deposit and all, was the one that started
   265	the argument.
   266	
   267	Riverside and Downtown send that line to different tax desks. Those
   268	desks only answer to the short names on the shop network, not the
   269	painted signs on the door, and the number that comes back is what has
   270	to sit on the invoice — not a percentage someone typed into the
   271	booking, and not last year's rate remembered from the other shop. A
   272	Downtown drone invoice that looked like a Riverside weekend was one of
   273	the fights; so was a Riverside lens quote where someone had typed the
   274	other city into the request and Downtown tax showed up.
   275	
   276	The insurance bureau charges a hull rider on cinema drones only, and
   277	they bill it by the day now — a working week on the Pier drone costs
   278	more cover than three days on the Downtown one, and the till has to
   279	tell the bureau how many days are on the paper or the bureau will not
   280	quote at all. Someone still managed to put a hull line on a tent, and
   281	someone else paid the drone without the bureau ever binding the policy
   282	because the signature on the bind did not match what the bureau had
   283	issued.
   284	
   285	The weekend desk counts every Saturday and every Sunday on the paper,
   286	each one, so a Saturday-and-Sunday pair costs exactly twice what a lone
   287	Saturday does; the old till charged one flat weekend line however many
   288	weekend days were on the slip, and on a long hire that was money we
   289	never billed. A paper that was only Saturday still owes that line —
   290	the old till treated a lone Saturday like a weekday. An adjacent
   291	Saturday-Sunday on the lens once looked like two weekday days plus tax
   292	and deposit, and finance caught it. Midweek spans do not pick it up at
   293	all.
   294	
   295	## Copies, punches and the diary
   296	
   297	The notice desk is supposed to hold a copy of every paid ticket the
   298	moment Stripe clears, with the same kit line, tax, hull, and weekend
